name: Autosomal Dominant Focal Dystonia, DYT25 Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Focal Dystonia

criteria.description: Presence of sustained or intermittent muscle contractions causing abnormal, often repetitive, movements or postures localized to a single body region
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Identification of pathogenic variant in the ANO3 gene (DYT25 locus)
Exclusion of secondary causes of dystonia such as drug-induced or structural brain lesions

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of focal dystonia with positive family history and genetic confirmation of ANO3 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for ANO3 mutations is essential for definitive diagnosis.

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; exclusion of metabolic causes
imaging: Brain MRI typically normal; used to exclude structural lesions

distinguishingFeatures: Focal neck involvement without family history

redFlags: Onset before age 10 suggesting alternative diagnosis
Presence of cognitive decline or seizures
references: Mencacci NE, et al. The role of ANO3 mutations in focal dystonia. Neurology. 2015.
Orphanet: Autosomal dominant focal dystonia, DYT25 type. ORPHA:329466.
Albanese A, et al. Phenomenology and classification of dystonia: a consensus update. Mov Disord. 2013.
